indicators.note: the drink word sits outside, wrapping the word for soft

parts.note: to sup is to drink
low, as in a low voice, means soft

explanation.surface: Someone relaxes with a fizzy pop, sipping it outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft drink' looks like one item, lemonade or cola, but the two words split and do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease off and stop rushing is to take things more slowly, a kind of relaxing.

clue.text: Hungarian composer against entering English Channel port

indicators.note: the short word for against goes into the composer's name

parts.note: Franz Lehar was the Hungarian composer of The Merry Widow
V, short for versus, means against

explanation.surface: A Hungarian composer, opposed to the plan, arrives at a port on the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: V (against) goes inside LEHAR, and E (English) follows. 'English Channel' looks like one name, but English supplies a letter and 'Channel port' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Havre is a major French harbour town on the coast facing England across the Channel.

explanation.surface: A loss of appetite or longing.
explanation.definitionFit: Want can mean a lack of something (for want of) and also a wish or longing for it.

clue.text: Hold check on amateur in possession of prize money

indicators.note: the prize money word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a purse is the sum of money offered as a prize, as in boxing
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: A ruling clamps down on amateur athletes keeping their winnings.
explanation.definitionFit: A purchase is a firm grip or foothold, as when a climber's boot finds purchase on rock.

clue.text: He moans when it's muddy around quarters

indicators.note: the word for muddy goes around the letters for quarters

parts.note: miry means boggy or muddy
S and E are two compass points, or quarters

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles whenever the ground near their lodgings is muddy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarters' looks like lodgings, but it means points of the compass.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a misery, or old misery, is a gloomy person who is always complaining.

indicators.note: the pole letter is taken into the middle of the word for gloomy

parts.note: moody means sullen or gloomy
N, the north pole, is a pole

explanation.surface: A man from Poland gets lost in a melancholy verse.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside MOODY. 'Pole' looks like a man from Poland, but it is the north pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A monody is a lament or elegy for a single voice, a mournful kind of verse.

indicators.note: putting out the letters means laying them out again in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A factory issues a new price list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a factory, but it is the definition, a living plant. The letters of NEW PRICES are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The screw pine, or pandanus, is a tropical tree with spirally arranged leaves.

indicators.note: not quite the whole word: its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a revolver is a pistol, a shooter in slang

explanation.surface: A gunman's turn has not quite come.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the last letter, R, from REVOLVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolve is to go round in a circle, to rotate or spin.

clue.text: Henry in longer version of opera?

indicators.note: a new version of these letters is a rearranged form

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A drawn-out production of an opera has Henry in it.
explanation.walkthrough: H, IN and LONGER are rearranged together. The question mark flags that the answer is one particular opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Lohengrin is Wagner's opera about the swan knight.

explanation.surface: A scatterbrained fair-haired woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the punning second reading: a blonde has a pale-coloured head of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Giddy describes a faint, swimming feeling; read literally, a fair-haired person has a pale-coloured head.

parts.note: R, for right, is a direction
over means left over, remaining

explanation.surface: A wanderer takes whichever route is still open.
explanation.definitionFit: A rover is a wanderer who roams from place to place.

indicators.note: organised means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Organised games irritate a man named Antony.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of RILES ANTONY are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Real or royal tennis is the old indoor court game from which lawn tennis came.

explanation.surface: Hand over the spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Give means springiness or elasticity (a mattress with some give), and also to hand something over.

parts.note: Ghosts is a drama by Ibsen, but read as spectres it suggests shades on stage: a theatre piece made of silhouettes

explanation.surface: Ibsen's Ghosts is an example of theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ghosts' looks like only Ibsen's drama, but ghosts are also shades, so a play about them is a play of shades.
explanation.definitionFit: A shadow play is a show of silhouettes cast on a screen by puppets or hands.

clue.text: Guess article is in metal casing

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: the metal word forms a casing round the short word is

parts.note: ore is rock from which metal is extracted

explanation.surface: Someone guesses which object is inside a metal case.
explanation.definitionFit: To theorise is to speculate or form a hypothesis, a kind of educated guess.

clue.text: Rest, dreaming endlessly about meeting the Queen

indicators.note: about means the letters are moved around into a new order
endlessly means the last letter of dreaming is taken off

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone at rest dreams endlessly of meeting the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' drops the last letter of the printed word, and 'about' shuffles what remains to REMAIND before the Queen's letters follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is what is left over, the rest of something.

clue.text: One with contract that couldn't be better

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a deal is an agreement or contract

explanation.surface: A man signed to a contract is in the perfect position.
explanation.definitionFit: Something perfect is beyond improvement, as good as it can be.

parts.note: double-speak usually means evasive language, but here it is talk between two people

explanation.surface: Deliberately misleading language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double-speak' looks like evasive jargon, but read literally it means speech by two parties.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialogue is a conversation between two people, talk in pairs.

clue.text: European then invested in premier race venue

indicators.note: the word for then is put inside the abbreviation for premier

parts.note: PM, prime minister, means premier
so can mean then, as in 'so you agree'

explanation.surface: A European then puts money into a leading racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs in Surrey is the English racecourse where the Derby is run.

indicators.note: the word for cult takes in the other letters

parts.note: a sect is a religious cult
US means American
P, a penny, stands for money

explanation.surface: A shady cult takes cash from America.
explanation.definitionFit: Something suspect is questionable or of doubtful honesty.

clue.text: Way of communicating what's vital energy policy

parts.note: life means vitality, liveliness
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A government's energy policy is said to be essential.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifeline is a means of staying in contact, often the only one, like a rope to a diver.

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is said to be in
tense means strained or stressed

explanation.surface: A powerful batsman is under pressure at the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means extreme or powerful in degree.

parts.note: a business that folds fails
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French silk fabric is folded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fold' looks like a crease in fabric, but it means fail, as a company does.
explanation.definitionFit: Faille is a soft, slightly ribbed woven cloth, often of silk.

indicators.note: to order means the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Someone plans to order a special bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb, intend, but it is the definition, nasty. The letters of SPECIAL BED are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Despicable means contemptible or low, as a mean act is.

indicators.note: a comeback sends the word for mad back the other way

parts.note: nuts means crazy, mad

explanation.surface: A boxer scores a knockout in a crazy comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to daze someone with a blow, leaving them senseless.

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son

indicators.note: the word for tame loses its tail, its last letter

parts.note: meek means docile, tame

explanation.surface: A boy's pet duck has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: S is followed by MEEK without its last letter, K. 'Duck' looks like the pet, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The smew is a small diving duck; the smee is an old name for the wigeon or a similar duck.

indicators.note: the word for no more surrounds the letter for Rex

parts.note: dead means no longer living, no more
R stands for Rex, the king

explanation.surface: Someone fears the king is no longer alive.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great fear or apprehension.

clue.text: Light metal magnets realigning connective tissue

parts.note: Li is the chemical symbol for lithium, the lightest metal

indicators.note: realigning means the letters are rearranged in a new line

explanation.surface: Lightweight magnets are used to reset connective tissue.
explanation.walkthrough: LI is followed by the letters of MAGNETS rearranged as GAMENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ligaments are bands of tough fibrous tissue joining bones together.

indicators.note: listening means the word for grim is heard spoken

parts.note: stern means severe, grim

explanation.surface: An English writer produces gloomy reading.
explanation.walkthrough: STERN, said aloud, sounds like the name of the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne was the 18th-century English author of Tristram Shandy.

indicators.note: the letters come straight out of these words run together

explanation.surface: A team withdraws from an elite contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across LEVEL EVENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket or football side has eleven players, so the number stands for a team.
